summary.headline: Solar Industries to acquire Omnia Holdings (South Africa) on an all-cash, 100% basis, funded by debt; ~$1.35bn deal value cited, FY28 leverage target below 2x EBITDA.
summary.overview: This was a business update call on the proposed acquisition of South Africa's Omnia Holdings Limited by Solar SA Investments (wholly owned step-down subsidiary), held as a transaction-only call, with no questions on core Solar operations taken. Management framed the deal as creating an integrated global explosives and blasting platform, adding mining (BME brand) and agriculture/agritech businesses, with benefits expected to be visible from FY28. Funding will be all-cash, through debt at Omnia level plus Solar-group debt and internal accruals, with no equity issuance planned. Management guided to combined FY28 revenue of about INR30,000-32,000 crore and EBITDA of INR6,800-7,000 crore, and said net debt/EBITDA will stay below 2x. Many figures are management estimates pending shareholder and regulatory approvals, and structuring is not finalised.

financial_highlights.change: Management projection; 17-20% growth to ~INR16,500 crore in FY28

financial_highlights.metric: Estimated FY28 total debt (acquisition plus regular)

financial_highlights.change: Figure raised by analyst, not confirmed by management

segments.name: Omnia Mining (BME brand)
segments.commentary: Covers opencast mining, bulk explosives, electronic and digital blasting, and mining chemicals; BME EBITDA margin cited at ~13-14%. Management expects the mining business to exceed INR7,000 crore in the next couple of years.

segments.name: Omnia Agriculture
segments.commentary: Crop nutrition, biological and biostimulant products (Nutriology model, AgriBio) with nitric acid and ammonium nitrate plants; a new 5,000-ton ammonium nitrate storage tank has doubled storage capacity. Management calls it a new, complementary vertical for Solar, with no plan to expand agriculture into India.

segments.name: Solar Africa base
segments.commentary: Solar's Africa revenue is ~$300 million; management expects combined African mining sales to reach $900 million to $1 billion. Problast (acquired 2024) adds down-the-hole drilling and blasting services.

guidance_outlook: Combined FY28 revenue expected at ~INR31,000-32,000 crore (Solar ~INR16,500 crore plus Omnia at least INR15,000 crore).
Combined FY28 EBITDA target INR6,800-7,000 crore, with synergies and operational efficiencies; EBITDA margin 22-23%.
Net debt/EBITDA to remain below 2x at all times, per management; debt repayment timing to depend on financial planning.
Benefits expected to become visible from FY28; distribution footprint to rise from 90 to ~110 countries and manufacturing from 11 to 25+ countries.
Management reiterated defence capex of ~INR12,000 crore announced two years ago, with defence capital allocation to rise.
capex_capacity: Omnia has nitric acid and ammonium nitrate production facilities, described as the largest and most reliable in the region.
New 5,000-ton ammonium nitrate storage tank recently added, doubling Omnia's storage capacity.
Solar's defence capex programme of ~INR12,000 crore is being executed aggressively, per management.
Transaction subject to shareholder and statutory approvals; structuring to be finalised afterwards.
demand_pricing: Management expects explosives global EBITDA margins of ~18-19%, against BME's ~13-14%; sees headroom via ammonium nitrate supply, initiating systems sales and Problast services.
Export and distribution expansion via BME into Canada, Australia, Indonesia and the US; management said entering a new geography takes 4-5 years.
Solar described as the largest producer of packaged explosives globally; BME distribution to be used to push Solar initiating systems and packaged explosives.
Management could not give market share figures for South Africa, North America or Brazil, citing lack of published data.

qa_highlights.question: How will the SADC value chain (Solar's South African plants, Problast, Omnia upstream) be integrated?
qa_highlights.answer: Omnia's ammonium nitrate and explosives capacity, Solar's initiating systems business (filling a gap at Omnia) and Problast's down-the-hole services together add value across three value-chain layers.

qa_highlights.question: What peak net debt/EBITDA is planned and how quickly will the debt be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt will not exceed 2x EBITDA; FY28 EBITDA of INR6,800-7,000 crore and debt of INR10,000-11,000 crore imply leverage below 2x. No specific repayment timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the deal be funded by equity, and does it dilute the defence focus?
qa_highlights.answer: No equity issuance is planned at parent or subsidiary level; funding will come from internal accruals and debt. Defence capital allocation will not fall and will rise over time.

qa_highlights.question: Will the agriculture business stay in South Africa or expand into India?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; no intention to expand agriculture into the Indian market for now, with technology-driven products to be used wherever Solar operates.

qa_highlights.question: Why do consolidated FY28 turnover numbers look low versus the analyst's INR34,000-35,000 crore estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR31,000-32,000 crore, using Solar ~INR16,500 crore and Omnia at least INR15,000 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the deal result in 100% ownership given Omnia's JSE listing?
qa_highlights.answer: The agreement is for 100% of Omnia, subject to shareholder and government approvals; no further detail was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is Australia or any other geography under-indexed and a growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on India and Africa; Australia is not an immediate priority, though BME already sells initiating systems there.

risks_watch: Shareholder, regulatory and government approvals pending; funding and structure not yet finalised.
Debt-funded deal increases leverage; FY28 net debt/EBITDA below 2x is management's estimate, not a verified figure.
Country and operational risk from managing multiple geographies, as acknowledged by management.
Omnia's agriculture business is a new vertical for Solar, with unclear strategic fit.
Synergy and margin uplift (BME from ~13-14% toward ~18-19%) are unquantified and depend on integration.
Management declined to comment on Solar's standalone operations, so no current-quarter operating update was given.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on the strategic rationale and FY28 targets, but cautious on specifics: management repeatedly deferred structuring, funding details and market share until approvals are obtained. Answers on leverage were given as broad ranges rather than firm numbers.
key_quotes: The strategic rationale for this proposed acquisition of South Africa's Omnia Holdings Limited is to create a most integrated global platform for commercial explosives and blasting solutions.
So in any situation, the EBITDA, if you take the EBITDA and debt position, it will always be lower than two.
We are not planning to raise any equity through any kind of dilution in any of the parent company or subsidiary.

adds.what: New 5,000-ton ammonium nitrate storage tank at Omnia (doubles Omnia storage capacity)

growth.why: Management guides combined FY28 revenue of INR31,000-32,000 crore (Solar ~INR16,500 crore plus Omnia at least INR15,000 crore) and Solar FY27 revenue ~INR14,000 crore, backed by an acquisition of Omnia (pending approvals, structuring not finalised) plus a commissioned 5,000-ton ammonium nitrate storage tank; no quarterly growth figures or current utilisation were given.
